rows.derivation: The rule's only consequence is 'the result of the statement is undefined'. No output is required, so any expected value a golden pinned would be invented, not derived.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.10 "When the data items are not described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is undefined" -> OK §14.6.10 1)
rows.notes: Undefined-result rule, the same treatment as DRV-GR-14.9.20.4-9 in CONFORMANCE.md §8. CONFORMS-but-untested is the correct end state.

rows.derivation: Each statement uses one entry as both sender and receiver, and the expected value is the result with a separate copy of the sender. ADD A TO A (7) gives 0014. MULTIPLY B BY B (3) gives 0009. ADD N N N TO N (10): the initial evaluation is 30, plus 10 gives 0040; storing after each addend would give 80. DIVIDE N INTO N gives 0001. SUBTRACT N FROM N gives 0000. COMPUTE C = C*2 + C/5 (5) gives 11.00, displayed C=01100. MOVE E(I) TO E(J) with I=J=2 leaves XYZ042. MOVE G TO G leaves ABCD1234.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.10 "When the data items are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is the same as if the data items shared no part of their respective storage areas" -> OK §14.6.10 2)

cite.py --check 14.9.2.4 "the sum of such operands. The sum of the initial evaluation and the value of the data item referenced by identifier-2 is stored as the new value of the data item referenced by identifier-2" -> OK §14.9.2.4 1)
rows.notes: The ADD N N N TO N line is the one that tells a correct implementation apart from a naive one. The other lines pin the rule's no-sharing result for each verb.

rows.derivation: No PERFORM or GO TO names the input or output procedures, so they can run only through the implicit transfer. SORT GR11: the input procedure runs first (IN-PROC), RELEASEing CCC, AAA, BBB. GR14: the output procedure runs after sequencing (OUT AAA/BBB/CCC, OUT-END), then control reaches the next statement (AFTER-SORT). MERGE GR9: the output procedure runs over F1 (AAA CCC) + F2 (BBB DDD) giving MOUT AAA..DDD and MOUT-END, then AFTER-MERGE.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.3 "When a SORT or MERGE statement is executed, an implicit transfer of control occurs to any associated input or output procedures" -> OK §14.6.3 2)

cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 "If an input procedure is specified, control is passed to the input procedure before the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequenced by the SORT statement" -> OK §14.9.40.4 11)
cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 "If an output procedure is specified, control passes to it after the file referenced by file-name-1 has been sequenced by the SORT statement" -> OK §14.9.40.4 14)
cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 "If an output procedure is specified, control passes to it during execution of the MERGE statement" -> OK §14.9.24.4 9)
rows.notes: Creates L1C09S1.DAT, L1C09S2.DAT and the work files L1C09S3.TMP / L1C09S4.TMP.

rows.derivation: DECL-RAN / AFTER-READ: a READ at end with no AT END phrase transfers to the USE procedure (READ GR24 d), then continues after the READ. M-PARA / M-SECT: PERFORM of an empty paragraph or section acts as CONTINUE. SUB-U / M-SUB-FELL-OFF: the sub's last statement is not under the control of another statement, so an implicit GOBACK returns to the caller. M-SUB-EMPTY: a sub with no procedure division statements does an implicit GOBACK. AFTER-EXIT-PROGRAM: EXIT PROGRAM in a program that was not called is not a transfer. FELL-THROUGH: GO TO the empty paragraph X3 continues into X4. The main program then falls off its end (implicit GOBACK, exit 0).
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.3 "an implicit transfer of control to those procedures occurs as specified in 14.6.13.1" -> OK §14.6.3 3)
cite.py --check 14.6.3 "The procedure branching statement EXIT PROGRAM causes an explicit transfer of control only when the statement is executed in a called program" -> OK §14.6.3 3)
cite.py --check 14.6.3 "execution proceeds as if the procedure contained only a single sentence consisting of a CONTINUE statement" -> OK §14.6.3 3)
cite.py --check 14.6.3 "In these cases, an implicit GOBACK statement without any optional phrases is executed" -> OK §14.6.3 3)
cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "If the AT END phrase is not specified in the input-output statement, any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed" -> OK §14.9.30.4 24)
rows.notes: PARTIAL COVERAGE: the golden pins every sentence that can end normally. It does not pin the two fatal-EC-declarative sentences ('there is no next executable statement ... the run unit is terminated abnormally'). The corpus runner requires exit 0 and compares stdout only, so an abnormal-termination outcome cannot be a golden. That arm needs an exit-code/stderr test in the style of RunUnitTerminationTests (the adjudicator's xfatal/xfatal2 probes are the recipe). The director may want to count this row as covered only together with such a test.

rows.derivation: Line 1 'F X=x K=2': with K=0, MOVE FUNCTION L1C09G (FUNCTION L1C09F : 1). Step 2 (function evaluation) runs first: L1C09G bumps K to 1 and returns 'wxyz'. Step 7 (reference modification) then runs L1C09F: K=2, start 2, giving 'x'. Evaluating the modifier first would give 'w'.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.4 "function evaluation" -> OK §14.6.4 2)
cite.py --check 14.6.4 "reference modification" -> OK §14.6.4 7)
cite.py --check 14.6.4 "that evaluation is done in full before proceeding to the next step" -> OK §14.6.4
rows.notes: Line 1 pins this rule; line 2 of the same program pins GR-14.6.4-4. The golden is in 2002 because a side-effecting function-identifier needs a user-defined FUNCTION-ID.

rows.derivation: Line 1 'M X=x K=2': with K=0, MOVE S :: "GETV" (FUNCTION L1C09F : 1). Step 3 (inline method invocation) runs first: GETV CALLs L1C09B (K=1) and returns 'wxyz'. Step 7 then runs L1C09F: K=2, start 2, giving 'x'. Evaluating the modifier first would give 'w'.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.4 "inline method invocation" -> OK §14.6.4 3)
cite.py --check 14.6.4 "reference modification" -> OK §14.6.4 7)
rows.notes: Line 1 pins this rule; line 2 pins GR-14.6.4-5. The methods bump K through CALL L1C09B because a FUNCTION reference inside a class unit is COBOLNET1505, a known separate limit. The main program is placed first in the file: when a subprogram came first, the run entered it and printed nothing.

rows.derivation: Line 2 'S X=b K=2': E = abcd/efgh/ijkl, K=0, MOVE E (FUNCTION L1C09F) (FUNCTION L1C09F : 1). Step 4 (subscript) runs first: K=1, E(1)='abcd'. Step 7 then: K=2, start 2, giving 'b'. Evaluating the modifier first would select E(2) from position 1, giving 'e'.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.4 "subscript evaluation" -> OK §14.6.4 4)
cite.py --check 14.6.4 "reference modification" -> OK §14.6.4 7)
rows.notes: The row is 85+, but the golden is in 2002: the ordering can only be observed with side-effecting operands, and 1985 has no user-defined functions, so no 85 program can observe it.

rows.derivation: Line 2 'P X=x K=2': with K=0, MOVE PV OF S (FUNCTION L1C09F : 1). Step 5 (the GET PROPERTY PV method) runs first: K=1, 'wxyz'. Step 7 then: K=2, start 2, giving 'x'. Evaluating the modifier first would give 'w'.
citations: cite.py --check 14.6.4 "object property evaluation" -> OK §14.6.4 5)
cite.py --check 14.6.4 "reference modification" -> OK §14.6.4 7)

rows.derivation: COMPUTE B2 = ALL B"1" B-AND ALL B"0": both B-AND operands are ALL literals, which the rule forbids. The sibling line B1 B-AND ALL B"0" (one ALL literal) is legal and is not flagged: the diagnostic points at line 21, and a control with the illegal line removed compiled and ran, printing 0000.
citations: cite.py --check 8.8.2 "The two operands in a binary boolean operation shall not both be the figurative constant ALL literal" -> OK §8.8.2 4)
rows.notes: reject-at 2002 2014 2023. The .err is 'COBOLNET1511: both operands of a boolean operator shall not be ALL literals', which excludes 1511's other meaning (the shift rule). At 85, boolean operators do not exist and the source is rejected for that reason instead (not listed).

rows.derivation: FACTORY. IMPLEMENTS L1C09I, where L1C09I is defined in the compilation group and declared in the PROGRAM's REPOSITORY but not in class L1C09K's REPOSITORY. The factory's SPEAK conforms, so SR1 is the only violation. A control that adds INTERFACE L1C09I to the class REPOSITORY compiled and ran ('FACTORY SPEAKS').
citations: cite.py --check 11.4.3 "Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition" -> OK §11.4.3 1)
rows.notes: reject-at 2002 2014 2023. The .err is "COBOLNET0840: class 'L1C09K' (FACTORY): IMPLEMENTS 'L1C09I'" (the FACTORY arm of the shared 0840). The full message cites ISO §11.4.3 SR1.

rows.derivation: (a) FACTORY IMPLEMENTS L1C09J, and the factory has no SPEAK; only the OBJECT has one, which is the object interface. So the factory interface does not conform. (b) FACTORY IMPLEMENTS L1C09O, whose prototype SPEAK takes PIC 9(4), but the factory's SPEAK takes PIC 9(8), so it does not conform (§9.3.8.2.3). In both files SR1 is satisfied. Controls with the conforming factory method compiled and ran ('OBJECT SPEAKS' / '0007').
citations: cite.py --check 11.4.3 "Each method prototype in each implemented interface shall be such that the factory interface of this class conforms to all implemented interfaces" -> OK §11.4.3 2)
rows.notes: reject-at 2002 2014 2023. The .err files are "COBOLNET0841: class 'L1C09L': the factory interface 'L1C09J' requires a method 'SPEAK'" and "COBOLNET0841: class 'L1C09W', method 'SPEAK': formal #1: numeric description mismatch". The messages cite §9.3.11/§9.3.8.2.3, not §11.4.3 SR2 (the adjudicator judged this acceptable). Cosmetic: the mismatch message calls the implementing method's formal 'argument'.

rows.derivation: Main: XA ASSIGN TO "xadat", XU ASSIGN USING FNAME OF G, >>TURN EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH CHECKING ON in every program. Under the documented rule (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-72): E1 TO XADAT (device-name, same spelling), E2 TO "XADAT" (case ignored), E3 TO DISK "xadat" (device class dropped) and E4 USING FNAME IN G (IN = OF) are consistent, so each sub runs ('Ek RAN', 'Ek OK'). E5 TO "xadat.txt" (no host mapping before comparing), E6 TO "xbdat" and E7 USING FNAME (qualifier differs) are inconsistent: per CALL GR3 e) the call is not successful, so ON EXCEPTION prints 'Ek MISMATCH EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH' and the sub never runs. Then DONE.
citations: cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 "A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause" -> OK §12.4.5.3 1) b)
cite.py --check 14.8.4.4 "For each external file connector, the rules specified in 12.4.5, File control entry General rule 1 apply" -> OK §14.8.4.4

cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "If one of the rules listed above is violated and checking for it is enabled for the associated exception in both the activated program and activating runtime element, that exception is set to exist, the program call is not successful" -> OK §14.9.4.4 3)
rows.notes: This is the witness PB1530 asks for; it observes the documented choice through the EC. The row is 2002+, but the golden is in 2023: the compiler rejects '>>TURN EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH' below 2023 (COBOLNET0878 'introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2023'), and the only existing golden for this EC (2023/ec_external_file_mismatch) is also in 2023. It does not observe the rule at 2002/2014. Worth confirming that the 2023-only gate on this exception-name is right. EXCEPTION-STATUS output carries trailing spaces, which the runner ignores.
